note: Facts for 'The Labyrinth' (Pac-Man). Each fact's `basis` substring must appear in the source chapter's rendered text (tools/verify-pacman.js). Theme: the soul's passage through the maze of the dead.

facts.label: The weighing of the heart
facts.fact: In the Egyptian judgment the heart is set against the feather of truth — the weighing of the heart, the moral centerpiece of the Book of the Dead.

facts.label: The forty-two judges
facts.fact: The dead recited a Negative Confession before forty-two divine judges — 'I have not stolen, I have not killed' — one denial for each.

facts.label: Anubis at the scales
facts.fact: The jackal-headed Anubis steadies the scales while Thoth records the verdict on the soul.

facts.label: The Descent of Inanna
facts.fact: Mesopotamia's great underworld poem is the Descent of Inanna, in which even a goddess is stripped of everything at each of the seven gates.

facts.label: Queen Ereshkigal
facts.fact: The Mesopotamian land of the dead is ruled by the great queen Ereshkigal, in a dust-dim house where all the dead go alike.

facts.label: No paradise below
facts.fact: Unlike Egypt, Mesopotamia offered no weighing of the heart and no paradise for the righteous — the dead all shared one gloomy fate.

facts.label: Persephone taken
facts.fact: Greek myth tells of Persephone carried off to the underworld, sought by her grieving mother Demeter, and returned for only part of the year.

facts.label: Orpheus the singer
facts.fact: A mystery current traced itself to the mythical singer Orpheus, who by legend descended into the underworld to reclaim the dead.
